page.overview:
What is Borgin and Burkes?

Borgin and Burkes was an antique shop located at 13B, Knockturn Alley, owned by Mr Borgin and Mr Burke, who were known to deal with unusual and ancient magical artefacts. It had a shady reputation due to the fact that it was frequented by those with sinister intents, who were considered dodgy, as well as the greedy and money-minded nature of its founders.

At some point, Borgin and Burkes was used to carry out otherwise shady business and to sell objects of Dark Magic and other dangerous magical items. These items included: the Hand of Glory, an assortment of human bones sitting on the countertop, a bloodstained pack of cards, a staring glass eye, rusty, spiked instruments that hung from the ceiling, a hangman's rope, a cursed opal necklace, and an array of evil-looking masks that lined the walls.

Some way down Knockturn Alley at number 13B lay Borgin and Burkes, the most notorious of the alley's shops, which specialised in "objects with unusual and powerful properties", and particularly items that were both "unusual and ancient". Many of the wizarding communities' children were instructed by their parents not to venture inside. Molly Weasley banned her twin sons Fred and George from setting even one foot down Knockturn Alley, due to the dangers present.

The shop was quite large, dusty, and dimly lit, with a large stone fireplace, and was known to be frequented by families like the Malfoys. Its proprietors, Mr Borgin and Caractacus Burke, were smooth talkers known to buy magical objects for much less than they were actually worth, and sell them for far more. One dangerous item that the shop carries was the Opal Necklace, that was once on display in the front window. This necklace had a read the label, "Do not Touch! Cursed. Has claimed the lives of nineteen Muggle owners to date."
